questions.prompt: An ordinary user belongs to the SSPR pilot group but has not registered enough methods permitted by the policy. Why can the user not complete a forgotten-password reset?

options.text: Scope inclusion alone does not provide the required identity-verification methods.
options.explanation: The user must register enough permitted methods.

options.text: Every SSPR user must be an Azure subscription Owner.
options.explanation: Resource ownership is not an SSPR requirement.

options.text: Selected-group pilots cannot support password reset.
options.explanation: Selected groups are a supported rollout approach.
SSPR specifically supports eligible password-reset operations.

questions.prompt: A synchronized user's cloud password reset must update on-premises AD DS. Which capability is required beyond ordinary password hash synchronization?

options.text: Supported password writeback with its permissions and policy enabled.
options.explanation: It sends the reset back to the on-premises directory.

options.text: Only the existing password hash synchronization.
options.explanation: That does not provide the required reverse reset path.
Registration supplies verification methods; it does not configure the cloud-to-AD password writeback path.

options.text: Enable SSPR for the user but leave writeback disabled.
options.explanation: SSPR eligibility alone does not send resets to on-premises AD.

questions.prompt: You are configuring recovery authentication methods for a new Entra SSPR deployment after the legacy-method policy deprecation. Which policy should you use?

options.explanation: It replaces legacy MFA/SSPR method management.

options.text: Only the deprecated legacy SSPR methods policy.
options.explanation: Current guidance directs administrators to the unified methods policy.

options.text: Only a Conditional Access policy requiring MFA.
options.explanation: Conditional Access can require authentication but does not replace the method-enablement policy.

options.text: Only the user's registered Security info entries.
options.explanation: Registration records available methods; policy determines which methods are permitted.
